gaps.sentence: It is almost ___ to park in the city centre (POSSIBLE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — parking is extremely difficult
gaps.explanation: The in- of 'possible' becomes im- before p: impossible. The context shows a negative meaning.

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: The new bypass will be ___ (BENEFIT) to thousands of commuters.
gaps.explanation: 'Be beneficial to' — the adjective follows the verb 'be'.

gaps.sentence: The audience was ___ by her performance (CAPTIVE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ate forms the verb: captivate. The passive 'was ... by' needs the past participle 'captivated'.

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'His'; note the -al suffix
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'refuse' is 'refusal' (-al noun); 'refuse' as a noun means rubbish.

gaps.sentence: He is one of the best ___ (SCIENCE) in the field.
gaps.hint: plural person needed after 'one of the best'
gaps.explanation: 'One of the best' is followed by a plural noun for people: scientists.

gaps.sentence: The prison was ___ , with three men in cells meant for one (CROWDED).
gaps.hint: too full — more people than the space allows (over-)
gaps.explanation: Three men in one cell means too crowded: overcrowded (over- + crowded). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.hint: person needed: someone who installs wiring
gaps.explanation: An electrician is the person who works with electricity; 'electric' and 'electrical' are adjectives.
